What We Did: Removed the title/salutation field (Mr/Mrs) from the customer form to keep it simple.
Replaced the old name fields with one 'Last name / Company name' field that works for both people and businesses.
Added a dropdown to mark a customer as a Fleet account or a Single customer.
Moved credit-card details into the Billing section as one tidy block and removed the old separate card fields.
Added a mailing address with a 'same as billing' checkbox so you don't have to retype it.
New customers default to Ontario, the usual province, to save typing.
Replaced real-sounding example names in the form with neutral placeholders.
Split phone numbers into clear Cell, Business and Home fields.
The customer and vehicle forms now use a clear 'Save' button.

Task: Package shows as one total on the invoice
What We Did: On the customer's invoice a package appears as a single bundled total, listing the items but not their individual prices.

Task: Add multiple packages to a job
What We Did: A single job can now include more than one package.
Transmission and differential services can be included inside packages on jobs.
Added two new staff roles — Supervisor and Technician — for more precise job assignment and access.
Staff can sign in with a simple username instead of an email address.
Rebuilt the screen where an Admin turns each page on or off for a user, so access is easier to manage.
Inventory now tracks how many of each part are on hand at each shop; only senior roles can change the counts.
Added an easy start/end-time picker (hour, minute, AM/PM) to record when a job started and finished.
Added an email field to the customer record.
Expense costs can be entered with extra decimal places for accurate part costing.
Each user has a profile page to update their name and change their password.
The 'customer-supplies labour' fee and counter premium can be set on each individual part, not just one global value.
Moved the vacation-pay setting out of Pricing and into Payroll, where it belongs.
Split the MHSW environmental fee into what you pay (Buy) and what you charge the customer (Sell).
Jobs have a dedicated Labour line so labour is recorded separately from parts.

Task: Pick service/labour items on a job
What We Did: You can choose predefined service/labour charges from a list when building a job.

Task: Choose price tier when adding a part
What We Did: When adding a part to a job you pick which price to charge: With Service, Without Service, or Over the Counter.
The Advisor dropdown shows only people who work at that job's location.
Changing an item's quantity inside a package updates that line's total automatically.
Created an 'Admin' account type with access to everything, including Settings.
The Owner runs the business but no longer sees Settings — that is now the Admin's job.
Managers can view customers and data across every location, not just their own.
Supervisors also get all-location access by default.
Tidied up the login page layout.
The MHSW fee is now built into a part's cost and shown consistently everywhere.
Fixed the math so Sell MHSW is added to the cost first, then the margin is applied, then the list price is worked out.
Reordered the part fields to Buy MHSW, Sell MHSW, then Cost for a clearer entry flow.
Defined the Over the Counter price as the part's list price.
Defined the With Service price as total cost plus the service charge.
Defined the Without Service price as linked labour plus the list price.
Renamed the confusing 'Counter premium' field to the clearer 'Service charge'.
Updated labels across the app to read 'Over the Counter'.
The service charge can be set to a negative number so it can act as a discount.
The MHSW amount now appears as its own column on jobs and printed invoices.
Sped up the parts catalogue so it loads and scrolls smoothly even with thousands of parts.
Staff can create and edit sales jobs at their own location.
A free-grease-only job is no longer shown as an unpaid invoice; the free grease is recorded as a $0 line.
You can record different details and multiple account numbers for a vendor at each location.
On a new expense, after choosing a vendor and location you pick which of that vendor's accounts to use.
Invoices pull the correct shop name, address, phone, fax and HST number from the job's location.
Merged the separate 'Description of Work' and 'Parts' sections into a single clear table on the invoice.
Double-checked that invoices show the correct location, HST number and date.
The oil-change price grid now lists only engine oils, hiding coolants and transmission fluids.
Reorganised the left menu into clear groups: day-to-day operations, then pricing, then finance.
Added loading spinners so it's obvious when a search is running.
Each part shows whether it is Active or Inactive, with a button to switch.
You can double-click a part row to open it for editing.

Task: Better customer search on new job
What We Did: Improved customer search on a new job — find people by licence plate, name, or any phone number, with clearer labels.
The activity log shows who changed what and when — including parts and pricing — and was fixed so entries actually show up.
Long tables now keep their header row visible while you scroll.
Added All / Active / Inactive tabs to filter the parts list.

Task: Warn before deactivating a stocked part
What We Did: If you deactivate a part that still has stock on hand, the system warns you first.
While typing a part number, the system warns you if it already exists.
A part marked 'bundled in a package' shows $0 on its own; if added to the same job again it uses the Over the Counter price.
Removed the tiny up/down arrows on number boxes so they aren't clicked by mistake.
In the job editor you can see and edit each package item's quantity and price, and the bundle total updates.

Task: Remove an item from a package
What We Did: You can remove an individual item from a package on a job; the package total adjusts to match.

Task: Add oil as a job line
What We Did: You can add an oil grade directly as a job line — choose bulk or gallon, set litres and price.
A job can record several payments (e.g. part cash, part card).
The free-grease offer can only be used once, within the customer's first 30 days.
Staff can only edit a job on the day it was created, and every job shows when it was last edited and by whom.
You can enter a negative price on a job line to apply a discount or credit.
Pressing Enter in a field no longer saves the form by accident — you save with the Save button.
The Upper and Lower technician dropdowns show only people at the job's location.
Fixed the With Service price so it still calculates correctly when the service charge is negative.

Task: Engine list filtered by vehicle make
What We Did: The engine list for oil-change auto-pricing is filtered to the vehicle's make (and shows all if none match).
Reworded the package upgrade/credit popup in plain language so it's clear what it does.
A 'Save and add new job' button takes you straight from creating a customer into a new job.

Task: Vehicle carried into the new job
What We Did: When you use 'Save and add new job', the vehicle is saved and pre-selected on the new job.
Made 'Add vehicle' a clear button that opens an add-vehicle window right on the job and then selects the new vehicle.
The system blocks saving a vehicle whose licence plate or VIN already exists.
While typing a customer name, the system warns you if a similar customer already exists.
On an expense you can pull parts from the catalogue and see each part's last buying price.
You can search those expense parts by number, brand or description.
Oil grades are listed alphabetically by name; the manual sort-order field was removed.
